input.brief: Project Ars - Open-source vector design editor with AI assistant and MCP support for live agent collaboration. Target audience: designers, developers, creative professionals. Key differentiator: AI-powered design with agent collaboration via MCP.

direction.name: Dressed as something else
direction.idea: Art-direct the subject as if it belonged to a different, more vivid category. A money app is sold like a streetwear drop. An industrial roaster is presented like a design object. Drilling hardware gets the calm of a watch brand. A parcel-locker service becomes a fairground of stickers. Choose the borrowed category by asking what feeling the audience is missing from this kind of product (swagger, calm, glamour, play) and which category owns that feeling. Then take its manners completely: its type, its pacing, its way of photographing things. The contrast between dull subject and vivid dress is what people remember.
direction.composition: Depends on the borrowed category, so decide it explicitly and write it in your notes. Fashion drop: one shouted condensed headline across the full width, a single cropped image under it, then product facts as a blunt list. Watch or perfume: a centred object on a dark field, a small serif name, very few words, long vertical pauses. Poster or zine: flat colour blocks, heavy type, tilted cut-out images. Museum: one item per screen on a plinth-like band of colour with a short label beside it. Whichever you choose, the page structure stays simple (four to six sections) and every section uses the borrowed manners, including pricing and the footer.
direction.typography: The borrowed category's type, fully committed: condensed and loud, or refined and small. No halfway.
direction.colour: The borrowed category's palette, which will be unlike the subject's sector norm. That mismatch is intended.
direction.imagery: Photograph the subject the way the borrowed category would be photographed. With the dealt set, choose images for attitude, not literal relevance, and crop them hard.
direction.richness: Attitude. The page has a recognisable voice from another world, applied to a subject nobody expected it for.
direction.pitfalls: Name the borrowed category in one word before you start, or the result is merely loud. The content must still be clear: what it is, what it costs, how to get it. Avoid borrowing from 'tech startup', which is the default you are escaping.

hero.name: Counter object, wide wordmark
hero.blueprint: Borrowed from a watch or perfume counter. One flat charcoal field. Centred slightly above the midline, a single low-key photograph of the object about 31% of the viewport wide (columns 5-8), 4:5, its own dark background matched to the field with filter: brightness(0.9) so it sits without a frame. Under it the name runs on one line as an ultra-wide wordmark spanning 72% of the width yet only about 45px tall: an extended face with letter-spacing near 0.6em, or a regular face stretched with transform: scaleX(2.4). Then one centred serif sentence at clamp(24px, 2.6vw, 38px). Then a single centred row at 15px with 48px between its three parts: one specification, the price inside the one solid light rectangle that is also the action, a second specification. The wordmark repeats small top-left and one text link sits top-right, both on 32px margins. The bottom fifth and both outer quarters of the screen stay empty and dark.
hero.mobile: The photograph grows to 70% of the width at 4:5, its top at 16% of the height. The wide wordmark spans the full width inside 20px margins at about 28px tall. The serif sentence sets at 6vw on two lines. The row stacks into three centred lines with the action in the middle at full width. The lowest sixth of the screen stays dark and empty.
hero.headline: The name as a very wide, very low wordmark on one line (up to 12 characters); the serif sentence beneath is the supporting line, up to 40 characters.

type.note: A tall American gothic taken from city signage, blunt and civic, over a plain public-service sans. Suits culture indexes, community projects, bars, sport clubs and local campaigns.

palette.name: Carmine field
palette.note: A deep red field bookends or fills the page, with white type and pale pink secondary lines; work shown in between sits on flat charcoal so it keeps its own colours. The button is a pale pink block with red type.

photos.title: Architecture
photos.note: structure, lines, bridges, facades and building interiors

photos.alt: Stepped white modern building corner rising into a pale blue sky
Red suspension bridge tower rising from fog above rugged cliffs
Tall pointed vaults and pale columns of a church interior
Curving glass and steel lattice roof in black and white

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Lit panel, dark row
sections.blueprint: One dark field, 96svh tall. Across its middle runs a horizontal row of five to seven interface panels, each a different true-size fragment marked data-ui (an open menu, an inspector, a composer, a chart card), 320–460px wide at their natural heights, vertically centred and 26vw apart. The row scrolls sideways with scroll-snap-type: x mandatory and scroll-snap-align: center, and can be dragged. Only the panel at the centre is lit: full opacity, in the product's light theme, the brightest thing on screen. The others sit at 22% opacity and are inert. The viewport's edges crop the outermost panels. In the gap to the right of the centred panel, top-aligned with it, a 24ch column gives its name at 24px in a light weight and two lines at 16px in a lifted ink; this text changes as panels arrive. There is no heading above the row.
sections.mobile: The row is 62svh tall; panels snap one per screen at true size, capped at 86vw wide, with neighbours showing 7vw at each side at 22% opacity. The name and its two lines sit beneath the row on the left margin and change with the centred panel. Swiping moves the row.

sections.name: Specimens on colour tiles
sections.blueprint: Each capability is represented by one object photographed alone and shown on a flat colour tile. Columns 1–3 hold the heading (two to four words at 40–52px), top-aligned, with a 30ch sentence beneath and nothing else down the rest of that column. Columns 4–12 hold a grid of five or six tiles in two rows with 10px gaps: tiles are 4:5 except one, which is double width at 8:5 and placed second in the first row. Tile colours rotate through three palette fields. Each photograph is centred at about 70% of its tile's height; on light tiles use mix-blend-mode: multiply so a white studio background disappears. Under each tile, outside it and aligned to its left edge: the capability name at 20px medium and one fact at 16px in the soft ink. No text on the tiles and no hover lift.
sections.mobile: The heading and its sentence sit on top at full width. Tiles become a two-column grid with 8px gaps; the double tile spans both columns at 8:5 and comes first. Names shrink to 17px and facts to 15px, still under each tile.

sections.name: Many into one
sections.blueprint: A diagram drawn with one repeated shape instead of arrows. The heading (two to four words on two lines at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px)) and a short paragraph at 17px sit in columns 1–4. Beneath, a wide inline SVG spans columns 1–12 at about 4.5:1. It is built from 120–160 small filled squares (or the page's own motif), each 10–14px. In the left third they are scattered loosely in two pale tones. In the middle third they are pulled into a tight horizontal ribbon three squares high. In the right third they fan out again into neat, evenly spaced rows in the accent colour. The eye reads disorder, compression, order, from left to right. Under the diagram, three text columns aligned to its thirds: a bold one-word name at 20px and two lines at 16px each; the words carry the sequence ('Gather', 'Reduce', 'Release'). No connecting marks.
sections.mobile: The diagram turns to run top to bottom: a 3:4 SVG with the scatter at the top, the ribbon as a vertical band in the middle and the ordered rows at the bottom. The three names and their text sit to its right in a 38vw column, each level with its zone.

sections.name: Plans that step up
sections.blueprint: Three plans as flat colour tiles whose heights step like a bar chart, so the bigger plan is literally bigger. The tiles sit in one row with 8px gaps, bottoms on a common base line, each 4 columns wide: the first 360px tall, the second 480px, the third 600px. Each has its own palette colour, no border and one shared radius. Inside, top-left with 28px padding: the plan name at 28px bold, the price at 56px beneath it, then what is included as plain lines at 17px (the taller tiles simply have room for more lines). The bottom 64px of every tile is a strip in a darker flat tone of that tile's colour, and the whole strip is the button with its label left-aligned. A heading of two to four words at about 4vw occupies the empty space above the two shorter tiles, top-left.
sections.mobile: Tiles stack full width in rising order, each as tall as its content, keeping its colour and its darker button strip along the bottom. Gaps of 8px. The heading leads at 9vw on two lines, and prices drop to 44px.

sections.name: A band per question
sections.blueprint: Each question owns a full-bleed band, and the bands alternate between two flat tones (ground and one step away, or two palette colours with their assigned inks) and butt together with no gap. Inside every band the same grid applies: the question in columns 1–5 at 28–32px bold, top-aligned with 56px of padding above; the answer in columns 7–12 at 18px with leading 1.5, the same padding, and 56px below. Bands are as tall as their content, so their heights differ, which gives the stack its rhythm. Four to seven bands. The heading is the first band: two to four words at about 7vw on the accent colour, flush left, taller than the rest at about 40svh with the words anchored to its bottom-left. All answers are visible; there are no toggles.
sections.mobile: Bands stay full-bleed and alternate. Inside each, the question at 22px then the answer at 17px, with 32px padding top and bottom and 20px at the sides. The heading band is 30svh tall with its words at 13vw at the bottom-left.

sections.name: One word is the button
sections.blueprint: The entire band is one link. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, about 60svh tall, contains a single verb of four to eight letters set at 24–30vw in the heaviest weight, tight tracking, sized with `clamp()` so it spans the content width on one line with its baseline 24px above the bottom edge. The `<a>` wraps the whole band; on hover and focus the field and the word swap colours instantly. In the top-left corner, at 20px, one sentence says what happens next; in the top-right, an arrow drawn as a simple inline SVG, 48px, points up and right. There is no other button anywhere in the section. In a page with a motif, the band's top corners take the motif's shape (a large radius, or a chamfer cut with `clip-path`). Keep the word honest: the action itself, not a slogan.
sections.mobile: The band is 46svh tall. The word is set at whatever size fills the width on one line; choose a shorter verb rather than going below 22vw. Sentence top-left at 17px across two lines, arrow top-right at 32px. The whole band stays tappable.

sections.name: Columns above, wordmark below
sections.blueprint: The footer inverts ground and ink and fills a whole viewport (min-height 100svh), arranged as three rows in a grid (auto 1fr auto). Top row, 40px from the edge: four small columns on the 12-column grid (address, navigation, social, hours or contact), each a plain list at 15–16px with its first line in the full ink and the rest in the softer ink. Middle row: empty. Bottom row: the wordmark alone, sized to run from the left margin to the right margin on one line. Set it as inline SVG text with a `viewBox` fitted to the word and `width: 100%`, or tune `font-size` in `vw` to the letter count, so it never wraps; its baseline sits 20px above a single line of legal text at 13px. With `position: sticky; bottom: 0` and a lower `z-index` than the page, the last section slides away to uncover it.
sections.mobile: Columns become two by two at 15px with 32px between rows, at the top. A gap of about 20svh follows. The wordmark spans the full width at the bottom; a name longer than ten letters stacks on two lines, each fitted to the width. Legal line beneath at 12px.

references.name: Moto Finance
references.idea: A metal card presented like a museum piece: lit by a single overhead light box in a black room, then orbiting through dim architectural stills.
references.hero: Black full-bleed 3D scene. A pale silver-lavender light panel, a trapezoid in perspective like a ceiling light box, occupies the top 20% and centre 55% of the viewport. The two-line uppercase headline, centred at 4.4vw in medium grotesk with tight leading, straddles the panel's lower edge so its first line sits half on light, half on black. In the exact centre a small metal card stands on a low plinth, only about 150px wide, surrounded by darkness. A light-grey pill button (about 250 by 52px) is centred near the bottom; the logo is top-left and a dark pill button top-right.
references.type: Neue Montreal only: weight 500 uppercase at 64px (4.4vw) with near-zero tracking and leading under 1.0 for headings, 20px sentence case for body, tiny caps labels in the footer. Three sizes; centred until the left-aligned footer.
references.colour: #080808 #edefef #c4cbd6 #e1e5e5 #2a2f3a — Black with cool silver-grey and no brand colour at all. One section inverts to pale grey-white with grey type; the only chroma is amber city lights and a blue atmosphere rim on the globe.
references.imagery: Rendered chrome card with an embossed profile medallion, a night-side Earth, and small dim architectural and fashion stills floating as tilted panels in 3D. Everything underexposed, cool and low-saturation.
references.layout: Full-viewport scenes stacked one per screen, each with a centred uppercase heading, an optional short sub-line and a pill button. One light interlude breaks the black. The footer switches to a left-aligned statement with link columns at the far right.

sections.description: Centred heading at the top with a two-line grey sub-line and a pale pill button directly under it. The lower 45% is the top arc of a night-side Earth rising from the bottom edge, about 75% of the viewport wide, with city lights and a bright blue-white rim on the upper right. Three small dark capsule labels with check icons float over and beside the globe at staggered positions, like status notifications.

A dark 3D room: about twelve small photo panels (roughly 70 by 90px, each tilted at its own angle, heavily dimmed) arranged in two loose rows across the full width, receding with blur. The card stands edge-on in the centre, much larger, catching a specular highlight. Later the card faces front at top-centre and a centred two-line heading with a pill button sits under it.

A pale grey-white band. Two tall columns of currency amounts in mid-size light-grey sans, one at a quarter and one at three-quarters of the width, each fading to white at top and bottom like slot-machine reels, with the centre rows darkest. Between them, three short centred lines of small black text. The bottom edge of the band reveals a dark photograph.

steal: Let a headline straddle the edge of a light shape so one line is half on light and half on dark.
Show the product very small in a large dark space in the first viewport, then let it grow as the page scrolls.
Use vertically scrolling columns of real-looking figures, faded at both ends, as a quiet backdrop for a three-line statement.
references.media: An 11s hero video of a CG metal card on a plinth covers the whole first screen and holds on its last frame. Then a pinned WebGL globe in the lower half under centred text, a 3D card centred in a depth cloud of small photo tiles dimmed to 30-40%, full-bleed sticky photographs with text docked in opposite corners, and a photo strip sitting on an index list; all low-key and desaturated, photos meeting the near-black ground through 200-300px fades, 0px radius.
references.motion: The intro ends in about 1.2s as the camera pushes in and the headline, nav and button arrive (load 9.9s), and Lenis then runs 32 ScrollTriggers: the globe pins for 2.5 viewports at scrub 1, the card turns in 3D across its section, the theme inverts to pale grey with the nav colour following, and benefit rows scrub in one by one. Lines rise by yPercent over 0.65s power3.out and leave over 0.45s power2.in, and headings rise from a blur over 1s power2.inOut.

references.name: Locker Land
references.idea: A dry B2B parcel-locker pitch dressed as a fairground of die-cut stickers, where the main navigation is a fan of five tilted illustrated cards.
references.hero: Post-red field overlaid with a faint lighter-red square grid. Small white brand lock-up top-left; a white pill button with a hard dark-red offset shadow top-right. Top-centre, a two-line sticker-style logo (cream letters, thick cream outline, small locker drawing) about 20% of viewport width. Beneath it a two-line centred white sentence at 18px; no larger headline. The lower half is a fan of five portrait cards with thick coloured frames and rounded corners: centre card upright, neighbours rotated about 8 degrees, the outer pair about 18 degrees and cropped by the viewport edges, each with a label tab overlapping its bottom edge. A two-line caption sits centred below.
references.type: apDisplay, a brand grotesque, is the only family: weight 500, sentence case, slightly tight. Body 16-18px; section headings in dark red reach about 5.9vw. The hero has no typographic headline, the sticker logo plays that role. Labels inside sticker tabs go bold.
references.colour: #dc1928 #fdf3db #952625 #e0a912 #5b7a94 #d46831 — Post red and cream alternate as full section fields; mustard, slate blue, burnt orange and maroon are reserved for card frames and badges. Warm, flat, no gradients.
references.imagery: Flat vector drawings (parcel, locker, hand holding a card) with thick cream die-cut outlines and hard offset shadows, plus candid photos of people at lockers placed inside arch-shaped cut-outs and wide rounded video tiles.
references.layout: Every section is a centre-stacked composition on a full-width colour field, with a pill-shaped sticky sub-nav top-centre after the hero. Sections are separated by ornament rather than whitespace: a red and cream checkerboard strip, a scalloped awning edge. Cards come in tilted rows of three or five.

sections.description: On red beneath a checkerboard strip, a dark-red pill with a dotted inner border holds the heading. Three statistics are scattered as tilted stickers instead of a row: a mustard circle, a maroon starburst seal with a cursor-arrow sticker overlapping it, and a slate-blue tag shape, each with a small parcel or locker illustration tucked onto a corner. Figures are large; captions are tiny and centred inside each shape.

On cream, the heading sits in a white rounded box with dark-red outline and offset shadow, hanging directly under the sticky nav. Below, three equal portrait cards in mustard, slate blue and orange, each with a dark-red border and hard offset shadow, containing an arch-shaped photo cut-out of people, a tilted name-tag sticker, a starburst date badge, two centred lines of copy and a small white pill button.

A centred locker illustration with icon stickers orbiting it, a centred heading and two-line intro, then a full-width two-by-two mosaic of video stills with no gaps and rounded outer corners. Each tile carries one large white rounded chip with a bold red word, placed low and off-centre. A hand-drawn orange arrow sticker overlaps the mosaic's top-left corner, pointing in.

Five stacked white pill-shaped rows in a centred column about 65% of the page wide, each with dark-red outline, hard offset shadow, question at left and chevron at right. A checkerboard strip then returns the page to red, where an oversized version of the sticker logo sits centred with a one-line copyright beneath.

steal: Turn the primary navigation into a fan of tilted illustrated cards in the hero, centre card upright and the outer ones rotated and cropped by the viewport edges.
Give every element the same die-cut sticker treatment (thick cream outline plus a hard, unblurred offset shadow in a darker shade of the background) so buttons, cards and badges read as one family.
Present statistics as differently shaped badges (circle, starburst, tag) scattered at angles rather than as three equal columns.

references.name: DialKit
references.idea: The headline is the demo: three floating dial controls from the product sit on top of the sentence and change its weight, spacing and effects live.
references.hero: Near-black viewport with no logo and no nav beyond a two-word audience toggle (active white, inactive grey) in 13px at top-left. A three-line sentence, centred, white, about 9vw with leading near 1.0, occupies the middle 60% of the width and sits optically centred. Three dark glass control chips, each roughly 300 by 80px with large-radius corners, a label on a lighter tab and a monospace value, float over the text at different tilts: one above the first line, one overlapping the start of the last line at lower left, one a segmented off/on switch at lower right. The chips blur the letters beneath them. The bottom third is empty.
references.type: Mluvka at weight 450 for the 128px headline (-0.02em) and 16px body; system monospace for control values, code and prompts. Section headings are only ~18px semibold, so the scale is one giant sentence followed by documentation-size type.
references.colour: #111111 #0b0b0b #262626 #ffffff #8a8a8a — Almost pure greyscale: #111 ground, #262626 code panels, white text, grey secondary. Colour arrives only inside demo recordings and syntax highlighting; a faint warm glow rims the control chips.
references.imagery: Screen recordings of interfaces being tuned with the control panel, shown as rounded tiles bent around a 3D cylinder; plus one large embedded demo card pairing a photo stack with its control panel.
references.layout: A full-viewport centred hero and a full-width curved carousel, then everything collapses into one centred ~680px documentation column with left-aligned text: small headings, tab rows, code panels, prompt blocks. It reads like a well-set README.

sections.description: A band of six or seven screen-recording tiles mapped onto the inside of a wide horizontal cylinder. Tiles in the centre face the viewer at full size; tiles toward the edges shrink, skew in perspective and fade into black, so the row reads as a curved cinema strip about 95% of the viewport wide and 150px tall, floating in empty black with nothing above or below it.

A single rounded dark card, about 680px wide and 650px tall, split in two. Left: a live demo with a title, a date and two overlapping photographs. Right: a narrow control panel of stacked slider rows, a spring-curve graph and toggles. A text link sits in the card's bottom-left corner. Directly below, a small heading with a tab row of package managers and a one-line code strip.

A docs-style stack in the same narrow column: a small semibold heading, a framework tab row (active white, others grey), one paragraph, then a rounded #262626 code panel with syntax colouring. A list of ready-made prompts follows, each a bold one-line label above a monospace prompt set in its own rounded panel, with about 30px between items.

steal: Place the product's real controls on the headline and let them alter the headline's own type settings.
Reduce navigation to a single audience toggle (human or agent) that swaps the page's content mode.
Wrap a row of screen recordings around a 3D cylinder so the strip skews and fades at the edges instead of running as a flat marquee.
